scientific_question: Does sequential sensing have measurable downstream advantage when the first observation identifies an otherwise latent reliable-expert mode, under a two-read budget and no generator regime labels at inference?

synthetic_causal_source.first_read_source0: Noisy mode probe, independent from the hidden binary target; value low in source mode0, high in source mode1
synthetic_causal_source.mechanism: Sensor1 informative for mode0, sensor2 informative for mode1, both share overlapping pooled reliability; third source is weak truth signal
synthetic_causal_source.test_regime4: Reverses first mode cue polarity without telling the learned candidate or cheap controls
synthetic_causal_source.test_regime3: New reliability strengths/noise with training cue polarity

test.relation_composer: Parity for even families, 2/3 majority for odd families

controls: strong public-anchors conditional empirical MSE nearest neighbors
simple static threshold on first mode probe
